content.title: About
content.content: Cheese ravioli are small pasta parcels filled with creamy cheese and served in a smooth cream sauce. The durum‑wheat dough gives them a firm bite, while the sauce adds a rich, velvety flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ravioli originated in Italy over 800 years ago as a traditional first‑course dish.
Typical cheese fillings combine ricotta, parmesan, and mozzarella, often with herbs.
Cream sauce is usually made from heavy cream, butter, and parmesan, sometimes flavored with nutmeg.
Ravioli are traditionally served as a primo (first course) in Italian meals.
Regional variations exist: Tuscany adds spinach, Piedmont includes mushrooms.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The cheese filling provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cheese supplies calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Both the dough and cheese deliver B1, B2, and B6 vitamins that aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Certain cheeses (e.g., ricotta) may contain live cultures beneficial for gut microbiota.

items.title: Balanced carbohydrates
items.content: The pasta provides slowly digestible carbs, helping maintain steady blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The cream sauce and cheese can cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The dish is rich in fats and calories, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to milk proteins.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Cream sauces often contain added salt; those with hypertension should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the ravioli hot, drizzled with the cream sauce. Garnish with fresh herbs, grated parmesan, or a light salad. Pairs well with a crisp white wine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked ravioli in the refrigerator for up to 2 days in an airtight container. Uncooked frozen ravioli can be kept for up to 3 months when vacuum‑sealed.
